title: Acceptance criterion
description: An objective pass/fail condition, tracing to the component it evaluates and the requirement it verifies. ⚠️ Approved 2026-08-22 after stage 7 was RUN (#144) — the second type added on demand rather than from a list, and the first where the stage's declared output and the demanded output agree. It answers the question neither a requirement nor a component can: a requirement says what must be true, a component says what implements it, and NEITHER says how you would know it worked.

allOf.$comment: A criterion recorded as failed must say what showed that. Nested inside allOf per #82.

then.$comment: A bare `fail` is an accusation with no basis. A `pass` may stand on a link or on nothing yet — see `outcome` — but a failure must at least say what was seen.

allOf.$comment: The lifecycle/supersededBy invariant, the same one `decision` and `assertion` carry, and nested inside allOf for the same measured reason (#82). ⚠️ ADDED 2026-08-28 BECAUSE A FAILED CRITERION HAD NOWHERE TO GO. ACC-0020 failed, its stated fallback was disproved by the measurement rather than confirmed, and the only ways to move the project on were to flip the outcome, delete the criterion, or exempt it from the handoff tripwire — all three of which destroy the record of what was measured. A criterion is retired the way a decision is: it stays, failed, and names the successor that replaced it. `setLifecycle` already wrote this field for every type; only this schema refused it.

then.$comment: A superseded criterion must name what replaced it. A retired criterion with no successor is how a failed measurement becomes a gap nobody can see: the tick disappears and so does the obligation.

else.$comment: Nothing that still stands has been replaced. Structural, so it belongs here rather than in the lint — every consumer would otherwise have to re-learn it.

statement.description: The condition, stated so that passing or failing it requires no judgment call. ⚠️ Stage 7's exit criterion is exactly this property, so a statement that reads 'the handoff should be good' is not a criterion — it is a wish with an ID.

evaluates.description: The component this criterion tests. Required and non-empty: a criterion that evaluates nothing cannot be run, and it is the edge #60's cascade traverses — its worked example is `acceptance-criterion -> component`.

verifies.description: The requirement this criterion demonstrates. Separate from `evaluates` because the two answer different questions — WHAT is being tested versus WHY it matters — and the handoff slice pulls the traced requirement along with the criterion (#19).

outcome.description: ⚠️ A RECORDED JUDGEMENT, not a derivation, and the distinction is deliberate. `assertion`'s verdict is derived because an evidence graph determines it (#96); a criterion's outcome is determined by somebody running it and looking. Deriving it from `evidencedBy` would require the polarity machinery assertions already have, and would make an acceptance criterion a second, weaker assertion. ⚠️ `not-evaluated` is the default and is a real state: a criterion that exists and has never been run is exactly what distinguishes a component that is IMPLEMENTED from one that is ACCEPTED (QST-0015).

evidencedBy.description: What was observed when it was evaluated. Optional on a `pass` because a criterion may be self-evident from the artifact graph; REQUIRED in substance on a `fail` (see the conditional), because a failure that records nothing cannot be acted on.

supersededBy.description: The criterion that replaced this one. Required when lifecycle is `superseded` and forbidden otherwise — enforced by the conditional in allOf, not left to the lint. ⚠️ This is how a FAILED criterion leaves the active set without its failure leaving the record. The successor must measure the disputed cost, not a relabelled version of the same claim; a successor that quietly widens the budget is the failure being edited rather than answered.

tags.description: Changing tags never invalidates an approval (#103).

x-ownsIrreducibleState.description: #41 applied in the stage-7 run, with consumers that were decided BEFORE the type was proposed.
x-ownsIrreducibleState.owns: A pass/fail condition and whether it has been evaluated. Neither a requirement nor a component can hold this, and an assertion cannot either: an assertion is a claim about the world, where a criterion is a test someone runs against a build.
traversedBy: #60 cascade — its worked example is acceptance-criterion -> component
#19 role slices — a slice pulls the traced requirements and acceptance criteria along with each task
task.acceptedBy — a task is done when its criteria pass

x-unresolvableTraceTargets.description: #75: none. component, requirement and evidence are all implemented and activated.
